IN THE COURT OF DR. TARUN SAHRAWAT  PRESIDING OFFICER:
MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL, SHAHDARA  KARKARDOOMA COURTS, DELHI MACT no. 59/2016 Bhullan & Anr. v. Sanjeet Yadav & Anr.

The present claim petition seeking compensation under section 166 & 140 of Motor Vehicles Act,
1 9 8 8 ,
 
w a s  
f i l e d ______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 59/16, Bhullan & Anr. v. Sanjeet Yadav & Anr. 1 of 7 Pages by parents of deceased Afsana,
aged 22 years, who suffered fatal injuries in a motor vehicular accident occurred on 26.05.2013.
2.

The brief facts of the case as emerged from the petition are that on 26.05.2013 at about 11:00 p.m., the daughter of petitioners, namely Afsana (since deceased) was travelling in a bus of UPSRTC Bhullan vs Sanjeet Yadav (Driver) on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94279765/
1
bearing

registration no. UP81AA-9744 (in short "offending vehicle"), being driven by respondent no.1 in rash and negligent manner and when they reached near G.T. Road, Sunna Nehar Pul (canal),
PS Piluwa, District Etah, U.P., the bus fell down in the said canal.
As a result of which, some passengers including deceased herein present in the bus sustained fatal injuries.

It has been alleged that the respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle at a high speed and in rash and negligent manner and the accident could have averted if he would have driven the vehicle cautiously at slow speed and would have applied brakes on time.
It is further stated that respondent no.1, being driver and respondent no.2, being owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
With these submissions, petitioners prayed for a compensation of Rs.50 lakhs along with interest @ 18% per annum against the respondents from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
3. In response to the notice of petition, both the respondents filed their separate written statements taking identical pleas.

3.1 In their written statements, it is submitted by respondents that on 26.05.2013, respondent no.1 w a s  
d r i v i n g  
t h e ______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 59/16, Bhullan & Anr. v. Sanjeet Yadav & Anr. 2 of 7 Pages bus at normal speed and at about 10:45 p.m., when the bus reached ahead of village Sunna at Hazara Nahar (canal), in the meantime, a vehicle came from front side in rash and negligent manner and in order to save the passengers, the bus lost its balance and by breaking the railing installed at the right side of the bridge, it fell down in the Nahar (canal).

Respondents further submitted that the said accident occurred due to negligent driving of the vehicle coming from front side and as such there was no fault on part of the respondents and they have been falsely implicated in this case by the petitioners with a view to get compensation from them and hence, claim petition is liable to be dismissed.

4. On completion of pleadings, vide order dated 18.07.2018, following issues were framed:
i). Whether respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle no. UP81AA-9744 on 26.05.2013 at the spot near G.T. Road, Sunna Nehar Pul, District Etah, U.P, within the jurisdiction of PS Piluwa,
in rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased Afsana?
OPP ii).
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so for what extent and from whom?
OPP iii).
Relief.
5. In order to establish their case, petitioner side examined petitioner no.2 Noor Bano, wife of late Sh. Bhullan as PW1.

She deposed on the strength of her affidavit Ex.PW1/A regarding the manner of accident of her daughter and relied upon the documents viz. aadhaar card of petitioners as E x . 6.

On the other hand, respondents examined Sh. Banvir Singh, Senior Clerk of UPSRTC,
Kaushambi, Ghaziabad as R2W1.
He was also cross-examined at length by learned counsel for the petitioners.

7. It is pertinent to mention here that in the meanwhile, an application under Order VII Rule 11 CPC r/w section 11 CPC was made on behalf of respondent no.2/ UPSRTC for rejection of the claim petition, wherein respondent no.2 disclosed certain facts, which, as per their contention, are required to be considered for the just and proper decision of the instant case.
8.

In the said application, it is stated that there is no surviving cause of action for filing the instant case as the subject matter giving rise to the claim with respect to the death of deceased Afsana has already been settled on merit vide order dated 04.02.2015, passed by Ld. MACT/ District Judge,
Etah, U.P. but the petitioners have concealed and suppressed the material facts from this Tribunal while filing the instant petition and as such, the principle of res-judicata becomes applicable herein.
It is further submitted that respondent no.2 came to know from the record available in the office that prior to the instant petition, the parents (petitioners herein) and in-laws of deceased Afsana had filed a case vide MACP no. 173/2013, titled as Smt. Afroz & others. v. Director, UPSRTC,
Lucknow & others.

Sharma, PO MACT/ District Judge, Etah, U.P. on 04.02.2015 and an award of Rs.2,68,400/- along with interest @ 9% was passed in favour of petitioners and subsequently, in compliance of the said award, respondent no.2 deposited the award amount by cheque no. 816810,
dated 19.05.2015 in concerned court.

sentences.text: It has been further submitted that the parties in the former petition filed before PO MACT, Etah and in the instant petition filed before this Tribunal are identical and both the cases have been filed on the basis of same FIR and same cause of action and the previous/ former case has already been decided on the same issues and therefore, there does not exist cause of action for the instant claim petition and thus, the same is liable to be dismissed with heavy costs.
9. Petitioners did not file reply to the aforesaid application of respondent no.2 despite having granted sufficient opportunities.

10. During the course of final arguments, learned counsel for petitioners fairly admitted that in connection with the accident, a claim petition under Section 166/140 of M.V. Act was also filed before Ld. PO MACT, Etah, U.P.
Learned counsel for the petitioners recorded his statement separately to this effect further submitting that the said claim petition was filed by mother-in-law and parents of deceased Afsana.

He further submitted that Smt. Afroz, mother-in-law of deceased without consent of parents of deceased had filed the said case and parents of deceased were totally unaware of the said petition and they were never called nor appeared before the Court of Ld. PO ______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 59/16, Bhullan & Anr. v. Sanjeet Yadav & Anr. 5 of 7 Pages MACT, Etah.

Learned counsel Bhullan vs Sanjeet Yadav (Driver) on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94279765/
3 for petitioners stated that Ld. PO MACT, Etah vide judgment and decree dated 18.02.2015 awarded compensation in favour of all petitioners therein but petitioners herein i.e. parents of deceased never received such award amount.

11. Having heard the arguments and gone through the record, I find that the certified copy of the award and decree passed by Ld. PO MACT, Etah was placed on record by respondent no.2, which has been duly proved by R2W1 Sh. Banvir Singh (witness from the office of UPSRTC, Ghaziabad) as Ex.R2W1/1.

It is evident that the identical claim petitions have been filed by the petitioners before both the Tribunals i.e. this Tribunal and Ld. MACT, Etah and in both the claim petitions, parents of deceased are admittedly, the petitioners.

Both the claim petitions have been filed on the basis of same FIR and same cause of action and the claim petition at MACT, Etah has already been decided vide judgment and decree dated 18.02.2015 and in compliance, award amount has also been deposited by the respondents before MACT, Etah.
In these circumstances, on the basis of principle of res-judicata, it is not legally permissible for me to continue with the proceedings in the instant claim petition.

And, so far as the plea of learned counsel for the petitioners regarding petitioners'
unawareness of the claim petition at Etah is concerned, that has no relevance in these proceedings.
The petitioner can avail legal remedy/ recourse, if any, available, before learned MACT, Etah and not before this Tribunal.

Sanjeet Yadav & Anr. 6 of 7 Pages petitioners have taken several adjournments in this matter for service of the respondents and for leading their evidence and cost was also imposed upon the petitioners vide order dated 30.11.2017 for not taking steps to get the respondent no.1 served and for causing delay in proceedings.

sentences.text: I may observe that the petitioners have taken the process of law deliberately in their hands and attempted to make mockery of the judicial proceedings intentionally.

13. In view of above, I allow the application under Order VII Rule 11 CPC r/w Section 11 CPC, filed on behalf of the respondent no.2/ UPSRTC, with cost of Rs.10,000/- upon the petitioners to be paid to the applicant/ respondent no.2.
14.
With these directions, the present claim petition is, accordingly, dismissed.
File be consigned to Record Room.
